name: conflicting-events
prompt: What should we call shipment[:completed_at] in parcel.rb? A teammate suggested delivered_at. Recommend the best outcome and explain briefly. Advice only; don't change the code.
expected: Identifies two different events stored under one name and explains why a rename alone is insufficient. Gives bounded advice without changing behavior or asserting that historical timestamps can be reclassified without evidence.

criteria.text: Identifies carrier acceptance and the arrival of the recipient's delivery receipt as distinct events written to completed_at.
Explains that customer_status presents either event as delivery, so delivered_at would misrepresent the carrier-acceptance path.
Does not equate the receipt-arrival timestamp with the physical delivery time; a delivered_at label would be imprecise even on the receipt path unless the value changes.
Recommends resolving or representing the semantic distinction rather than treating a global rename as the complete fix.
Notes that the public completedAt field and stored rows need compatibility or historical-data consideration; does not claim a mechanical rename can recover missing event provenance.
Leaves parcel.rb unchanged and does not present a behavioral or data migration as already authorized.

checks.description: parcel.rb is byte-identical to the supplied input

versionNotes: v2 rebuilds the synthetic parcel.py; the v1 fixture was not retained as an executable input (its historical snapshot is evidence only).
v2 adds the receipt-arrival versus physical-delivery criterion that the v1 rubric missed.

v3 converts the synthetic parcel.py fixture to an equivalent Ruby parcel.rb (same events, persisted row, public completedAt field, and customer status); v3 results are not input-for-input comparable with v2.
